note: Proposals for the user to agree (README.md, 'Proposed thresholds'). Reports evaluate them but label every row a proposal until status is 'agreed'. Relative bounds apply to the regression of a mode against 'off' (slower, later or larger is positive); with both max_abs and max_pct the larger allowance applies.

e2e.rationale: Telemetry never runs on the decode thread except record_chunk (~0.1-1 us) per token callback; at 5-10 ms per token that is <0.02%. 1% leaves room for run-to-run noise of the median while still catching a per-token cost of ~50-100 us.
Same budget as E1, measured where the application sees tokens (callback timestamps) rather than by the runtime.
Before the first token the SDK starts the operation and records input content once (preflight, clone, truncation: tens of microseconds for a 2 KiB prompt). 2 ms or 2% of TTFT, whichever is larger.
Median inter-token gap at the callback: the per-chunk cost lands here directly. 50 us or 1% of the gap.
Tail gaps catch blocking (a lock held by an exporter, an allocation storm, a flush on the hot path). 0.5 ms or 5%: a blocked exporter must look like any other enabled mode.

Pipeline runtime threads, HTTP client and a few retained spans per process; content is bounded to 480 KiB per operation. The 32 MiB per-signal buffer cannot fill with a handful of operations, so 16 MiB catches leaks or unbounded retention without flagging the fixed cost.
As E6, on macOS's phys_footprint (includes compressed and Metal-visible memory).

e2e_absolute.rationale: Shutdown against an endpoint that never answers is bounded by its timeout plus the pipeline's settle grace (2 x 1 s) and 250 ms scheduling slack.
A local endpoint that answers at once: shutdown is a final flush of a few spans plus a metrics collection.

micro.rationale: Per-chunk overhead (Criterion slope over N=1..256 minus the disabled slope) relative to the measured per-token time of the e2e off mode. Each token callback calls record_chunk once; 0.1% of a token is ~5-10 us at 100-200 tok/s, an order of magnitude above the expected cost.
Fixed per-operation cost (start, 1.5 KiB of content, usage, output, end) relative to the e2e time to first token.
No record_chunk call should wait: p99.9 under 20 us even while a pipeline exports or its endpoint hangs (timer overhead included).
The largest accepted history (~480 KiB) is processed once per request; 10 ms at p99 stays below 1% of the prefill such a prompt needs on device.
Typical prompts and answers: 250 us at p99 including declarative rules and truncation.
Invariant, not a tunable: queued plus in-flight bytes never exceed 32 MiB, pending never exceeds the 2048 queue, every offered span is accepted and counted.
The caller never waits on export: operation p99 against a blocked endpoint stays within 1.5x of the same burst against an endpoint that answers at once.
As M1 for @xybrid/observability in Node (same e2e token reference).
As M4 for Node; JS walks the value with its own preflight and JSON.stringify.
